viewsWelcome.contents:
Judge the AI's review, then ship it to your code platform.
[Sign in](command:codeVerdict.signIn)

codeVerdict.instanceUrl.description: Base URL of the platform instance this pod connects to. Empty uses the chosen provider's default host. The access token is never a setting — it lives in the VS Code secret store.

codeVerdict.agent.description: Id of the review agent. Agents are *.agent.md files; the model that runs one is stored per pod, not here.

codeVerdict.agentLocations.description: Extra directories to search for *.agent.md agent definitions, absolute or workspace-relative. Searched in addition to each workspace folder's default agent folder, never instead of it.

codeVerdict.severityFloor.description: Report findings at or above this severity.

codeVerdict.categories.description: Review categories the agent looks for.

codeVerdict.minConfidence.description: Minimum agent confidence for a finding to be reported.

codeVerdict.extraInstructions.description: Free-text instructions appended to every review request.

codeVerdict.autoAdvance.description: After a verdict, advance to the next undecided item.

codeVerdict.context.sectionBudget.description: Maximum characters sent from any single auto-derived context section. Missing or unusable values fall back to 4,000 characters.

codeVerdict.context.totalBudget.description: Maximum total characters sent as auto-derived context. Attachments and diffs use separate limits. Missing or unusable values fall back to 12,000 characters.

codeVerdict.context.maxLinkedItems.description: Maximum linked work items sent as auto-derived context. Missing or unusable values fall back to 5 items.

codeVerdict.context.includeTitle.description: Include the change request title in auto-derived context for new reviews by default. It can still be removed for a single run.

codeVerdict.context.includeDescription.description: Include the change request description in auto-derived context for new reviews by default. It can still be removed for a single run.

codeVerdict.context.includeLinkedItems.description: Include linked work items in auto-derived context for new reviews by default. Individual items can still be removed or restored for a single run.

codeVerdict.contextUsage.enabled.description: Show the selected model's estimated context-window usage before a review. Context and attachment budgets still apply when this indicator is hidden.

codeVerdict.harness.maxElapsedSecondsPer.description: Maximum time one review attempt may spend investigating before it must stop and report what it has. Raise it for a large changeset that needs more time; lower it to fail fast on a slow or unresponsive model. Missing or unusable values fall back to 1,800 seconds (30 minutes).

codeVerdict.harness.maxModelTurnsPerAtte.description: Maximum back-and-forth turns with the model one review attempt may use. Raise it for a large or unusually complex changeset that needs more investigation before the model can finish. Missing or unusable values fall back to 64 turns.

codeVerdict.harness.maxToolRequestsPerAt.description: Maximum tool calls — reads, diffs, searches — one review attempt may issue in total. Raise it for a large changeset with many files to inspect. Missing or unusable values fall back to 256 requests.

codeVerdict.harness.maxPromptKilobytesPe.description: Maximum size of one prompt sent to the model in a review turn, in kilobytes — everything in it, the review's own framing and the diffs and search results it carries. The model is told how much of this is left for the content it asks for, and requests that would not fit are not served that turn; nothing is spent on them and it can ask again. Lower it for a small local model that stalls on large prompts (128 is a reasonable value); raise it for a model that reads a very large prompt comfortably, at the cost of slower turns. Missing or unusable values fall back to 192 KB.

codeVerdict.harness.maxEvidenceMegabytes.description: Maximum cited evidence content — diff hunks, file excerpts, search results — one review attempt holds at once, in megabytes. Raise it if a large changeset's review is losing citations to evidence it read earlier in the attempt. Missing or unusable values fall back to 8 MB.

codeVerdict.harness.highRiskReservePerce.description: Percent of the attempt's turns, tool calls, and evidence held back for files the model did not pick to investigate but the host judged high-risk. Raise it if high-risk files are being skipped for lack of remaining budget. Missing or unusable values fall back to 20 percent.

codeVerdict.harness.verificationReserveP.description: Percent of the attempt's turns, tool calls, and evidence held back for final verification before completion. Raise it if verification is running out of budget on large reviews. Missing or unusable values fall back to 15 percent.

codeVerdict.harness.transientRetriesPerO.description: How many times the harness retries one tool call or model turn after a transient error (a network blip, a rate limit) before giving up. Raise it if reviews are failing on errors that would have succeeded a moment later. Missing or unusable values fall back to 3 retries.

codeVerdict.harness.checkpointCadenceToo.description: How many completed tool calls pass between checkpoints inside a phase, in addition to the checkpoint always taken at every phase boundary. Lower it to resume closer to where a long review was interrupted, at the cost of more frequent checkpoint writes. Missing or unusable values fall back to 10 tool calls.

codeVerdict.harness.retainedCheckpointsP.description: How many checkpoints are kept for one review's resume history. Raise it to be able to resume further back after a long or repeatedly retried review, at the cost of more stored data. Missing or unusable values fall back to 3 checkpoints.

codeVerdict.harness.maxActivityEventsPer.description: How many activity-log entries (plan updates, coverage progress, checkpoints) one review attempt keeps before the oldest are dropped. Raise it to see the full narrative of a long-running review instead of a truncated one. Missing or unusable values fall back to 1,000 events.

codeVerdict.harness.terminalAttemptHisto.description: How many finished review attempts are kept in history for one change request or changeset target before the oldest is pruned. Raise it to look back further after a review has been retried or resumed several times. Missing or unusable values fall back to 5 attempts.

How many days a finished review attempt's history is kept before it is pruned regardless of count. Raise it to keep history around longer for change requests you revisit infrequently. Missing or unusable values fall back to 30 days.

codeVerdict.harness.requireInspectionMin.description: The lowest risk level that must actually be read, not just classified, before a review can be marked complete. The default (medium) requires every changed file classified medium or high to be read; low-risk files — for example, documentation, specifications, and generated output — count as covered without being opened, and real source code is never classified low regardless of what the reviewing model proposes. Lowering this to low requires every changed file, regardless of risk, to be read; raising it to high lets medium-risk files count as covered without being opened too. Missing or unusable values fall back to medium.

codeVerdict.harness.scopeInvestigationTo.description: Keep a review's investigation to the files actually changed in its change request. Off by default: a review reads from a local copy of the repository, so reading an unchanged file to corroborate a finding costs a local file read and nothing else. Turn this on to withhold readFile, searchRepository and the AGENTS.md policy lookup that rides on the same capability, leaving the model only the change's own diffs and details — a smaller prompt and a review that cannot wander outside the change request.

codeVerdict.agentVoice.description: Voice of the generated summary comment.

codeVerdict.agentRun.firstOutputSeconds.description: How long the agent may take to produce its very first output after a request is sent. A large review sends a large prompt, and reading it before the first token legitimately takes longer than the gaps between tokens ever should, so this window is separate from (and longer than) the inactivity window below. 0 removes this limit entirely — the wait for the first output is then bounded only by the ceiling, not by the inactivity window.

codeVerdict.agentRun.inactivitySeconds.description: Give up on a review when the agent has started answering but no further output has arrived for this many seconds. The clock starts at the first output and restarts on every fragment, so a run that keeps streaming is never cut off however long it takes overall, and a slow start is judged by the first-output window above, not this one. Raise it for a model that thinks in long silences; 0 removes this limit and leaves the ceiling below as the only one.

codeVerdict.agentRun.ceilingSeconds.description: Long-horizon check on a review run. Every time this many seconds pass, the run is checked once: output arrived during the window and it continues, nothing arrived at all and it is cancelled. It never stops a run that is still producing, however long that run has been going. 0 removes the check.

codeVerdict.agentRun.maxConcurrent.description: How many reviews may run at once. Reviews beyond this wait their turn and start as earlier ones finish, so triggering one never refuses or cancels another. Each running review costs a separate model request against your Copilot allowance, which is what this limit is for. 0 removes the limit.

codeVerdict.notifications.quietMode.description: Quiet hours: demote everything except blockers and direct mentions.

codeVerdict.notifications.pollIntervalSe.description: Shortest gap between background checks for updates, in seconds. This is a floor, not the interval: one check costs several requests per watched repository plus one per review awaiting replies, so the effective gap grows with the size of the pod to keep background polling inside the platform's hourly request budget.

codeVerdict.shareAcceptRejectRates.description: Share aggregate accept/reject rates while keeping finding text and rationale local.

codeVerdict.changesets.trailer.description: Commit-message / MR-description trailer used to detect changesets. Branch-name matching is the fallback.

codeVerdict.changesets.branchDetection.description: Suggest a changeset when change requests across repositories share a source branch name. Trailer detection takes precedence; switch this off if reused branch names make it noisy.

codeVerdict.trace.api.description: Log every API request the extension makes — method, full URL, status, elapsed time, remaining rate limit, and the full request and response body — to the "Verdict: API" output channel, each line led by the local time of day. Credentials are redacted: request headers (Authorization above all) are never logged at all, tokens carried in a URL are replaced before the line is written, and any credential-shaped text inside a body is redacted too. A body larger than this channel writes whole is never silently cut — it says exactly how many bytes were left out.

codeVerdict.trace.rawPayloads.description: DEBUGGING ONLY — leave this off otherwise. Writes the full, unredacted prompt sent to the model and the full, unredacted text it replies with to the "Code Verdict: Agent Trace" output channel, and to nowhere else this extension writes. Nothing raw reaches anything Code Verdict persists — not the activity log, checkpoints, retained review details, the run diagnostics report, or the agent-trace.log file this extension writes itself — whether this is on or off. It is not a promise that nothing reaches a disk: VS Code captures the contents of every output channel into its own log directory, so while this is on, the prompts and replies shown in that channel are in VS Code's logs too.

codeVerdict.pods.description: Pods (named sets of watched repositories). Managed by the extension; edit through the UI.
